instructions: This is a machine-readable description of the project API, assembled by the framework from its own metadata. The index lists the modules; the details for a single module are available at /agent_manifest/cmsvc={name}. Request details only for the modules your task needs: a real project's full manifest does not fit into context. Rights are resolved per request, so the same address returns a different amount of data with and without a token. Before writing data, read the conventions section: the wire format cannot be inferred from the field descriptions.
module_unavailable: The module description could not be assembled: initialising its models failed. The field and action lists here are incomplete and must not be relied upon.

auth.scheme: Send login and password to token_endpoint and receive an access_token (a JWT valid for one hour) and a refresh_token (valid for 30 days). Then add the header "Authorization: Bearer {access_token}" to every request. When the access_token expires, send the refresh_token to refresh_endpoint — there is no need to store the password. Token issuing is rate limited: after five failed attempts the address answers with the rate_limited code and a Retry-After header.
auth.csrf: A request carrying the Authorization: Bearer header is exempt from the CSRF check. A cookie-authorised client must send the X-CSRF-Token header.

conventions: Field values carry an object index: name[0], tipe[0]. The index runs from 0 to n — the format is built for submitting several objects in one request. A bare scalar (name=Test) is rejected with the wrong_data_format code.
Field groups inside an object use a nested index: field[0][g].
Deletion: action=delete with an array of identifiers — id[]=2&id[]=3.

Parameters may be passed in path form: /{kind}/{param}={value}&{param}={value}. A trailing slash corrupts the last parameter value: /helper/input=Mos filters correctly, while /helper/input=Mos/ returns the whole reference list with no sign of an error. Do not add a trailing slash.
Fields from joined tables arrive in a list response as "table__field", with two underscores.

Every answer arrives in a single envelope: response (success or error), response_text, response_data with the payload, ids with the identifiers of created or changed objects, fields with the names of the offending fields in wire format, and response_error_code with the machine-readable error code.
On a validation error the fields key gives field names exactly as they must be sent back: fix the values and repeat the request.

errors.validation_failed: The data failed validation. The offending field names are in the fields key; fix them and repeat the request.
errors.unauthorized: There is no valid authorisation. Obtain a token or refresh it with the refresh_token.
errors.forbidden: This action is not permitted. Repeating will not help.
errors.not_found: The module, object or action was not found.
errors.wrong_action: The module has no such action. Check the actions list in the module details.
errors.wrong_data_format: The data is not in the format the framework expects. Most often this is a value without an object index: it must be name[0], not name.
errors.duplicate: Such a record already exists. Repeated saving was blocked.
errors.rate_limited: Too many requests. Wait as many seconds as the Retry-After header says.
errors.internal_error: A server-side error. The request may be repeated later.

crud.list: The list of the module's objects.
crud.view: A single object of the module by its identifier.
crud.create: Creates an object. The identifiers of the created records are returned in the ids key.
crud.change: Changes an object. The identifier of the record being changed is passed as id[0].
crud.delete: Deletes objects by an array of identifiers id[].
crud.lookup: A reference list: returns identifier and label pairs. The term parameter filters the output.
